newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Hillary Clinton calls E.Europe women to battle.
newsitem.headline: Hillary Clinton calls E.Europe women to battle.

text.p: U.S. First Lady Hillary Rodham Clinton, addressing a women's forum in Vienna on Friday, urged women from the former Eastern bloc to fight for more say in developing democracies, but warned it would be a tough slog.

"There cannot be true democracy unless women's voices are heard, unless all citizens are able to participate fully in the lives of their country," Clinton told some 1,000 delegates at the forum entitled "Vital Voices: Women in Democracy".
"But democracy is hard work. You can't flip a switch and expect to have a democracy you dream of," she added.

The three-day forum, which ends on Friday, was organised by the U.S. ambassador to Austria Swanee Hunt and has brought together prominent women from the United States, western Europe and the former Eastern bloc.
Hunt, whose posting to Vienna ends in October, has been a major financial contributor to U.S. President Bill Clinton's election campaigns.
The chief aim of the forum was to enable women leaders to share their expertise and devise clear strategies to boost the role of women in transitional democracies in Europe, she said.

Other prominent speakers included European Union Commissioner for Humanitarian Affairs Emma Bonino, National Bank of Poland President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz, the Vice-President of the Czech senate Jaroslava Moserova and former Lithuanian Prime Minister Kazimiera Prunskiene.
Clinton said many women were constrained by historical and cultural traditions, which prevented them from exercising free choice.
"(We must) use our voices to speak on behalf of all people, to give a voice to the voiceless," she said.
The forum was the first major women's congress since the U.N. Fourth Women's Conference in Beijing in September 1995, which the U.S. First Lady also attended.
Clinton, a high-flying lawyer, has been an outspoken critic of alleged human rights and population control abuses in China, as well as an ardent supporter of women's rights.
Reiterating an earlier message from Beijing, she told the Vienna forum: "Human rights are women's rights".
According to U.N. statistics, only 28 women have been elected heads of state or government anywhere in the world this century. Women hold around 13 percent of the seats in the world's parliaments.

Clinton pledged $3 million on behalf of the U.S. government to go towards democracy-building projects launched at the forum and urged the women to join forces to promote greater equality in their countries.

"If you go home and bring a message of solidarity that you have achieved here you will not change anything overnight. But your voice and work will create the conditions for change," she said to thunderous applause.
Clinton was scheduled to meet Austrian President Thomas Klestil and Chancellor Viktor Klima later in the day.
